proposed.before: Before he came of age he already stood eight feet two inches tall, cut an imposing figure, and bore the paired “sun-brow” and “crescent moon” lines on his forehead that physiognomists read as imperial signs.
proposed.after: Before he came of age he already stood eight chi and two cun tall, cut an imposing figure, and bore the paired “sun-brow” and “crescent moon” lines on his forehead that physiognomists read as imperial signs.
proposed.sourceReason: 八尺二寸 measures eight chi and two cun. The literal field preserves the two source units. Their numerical values cannot be carried into modern feet and inches without a sourced conversion.
proposed.sourceChinese: 年未弱冠，身長八尺二寸，姿貌雄偉，額有日角偃月重文。

proposed.before: He named Murong Lin minister of works and chief of the secretariat, Murong Fa central-army general, Yu Ba senior vice-president of the secretariat, Ding Tong junior vice-president, and distributed other posts accordingly.
proposed.after: He appointed Murong Lin minister of works and concurrent director of the Secretariat, Murong Fa general of the central army, Muyu Ba left vice-director of the Secretariat, and Ding Tong right vice-director. The others received titles and appointments of varying rank.
proposed.sourceReason: 慕輿拔 has the compound surname Muyu, also spelled out in s0178. The two Secretariat offices are explicitly left and right, and 自余封授各有差 covers the other grants and appointments.
proposed.sourceChinese: 以慕容麟為司空、領尚書令，慕容法為中軍將軍，慕輿拔為尚書左僕射，丁通為尚書右僕射，自余封授各有差。

proposed.before: Murong De appointed Murong Lin as minister of works and concurrent director of the secretariat, Murong Fa as general of the central army, Yu Ba as left vice-director of the secretariat, Ding Tong as right vice-director of the secretariat, and the rest received titles each according to rank.
proposed.after: Murong De appointed Murong Lin as minister of works and concurrent director of the secretariat, Murong Fa as general of the central army, Muyu Ba as left vice-director of the secretariat, Ding Tong as right vice-director of the secretariat, and the rest received titles each according to rank.
proposed.sourceReason: The full Chinese name 慕輿拔 includes both characters of the surname 慕輿. The later appointment in s0178 already uses Muyu Ba.
proposed.sourceChinese: 以慕容麟為司空、領尚書令，慕容法為中軍將軍，慕輿拔為尚書左僕射，丁通為尚書右僕射，自余封授各有差。

proposed.before: Yu Hu volunteered to ride north and learn Murong Bao's true situation; Murong De sent him off in tears.
proposed.after: Muyu Hu volunteered to ride out and learn Murong Bao's true situation. Murong De sent him off in tears.
proposed.sourceReason: 慕輿護 is Muyu Hu. 請馳問寶虛實 is his request to ride to learn the facts about Bao. The direction north comes in the next unit.
proposed.sourceChinese: 慕輿護請馳問寶虛實，德流涕而遣之。

proposed.before: Yu Hu requested to gallop and inquire into Murong Bao's truth and falsehood, and Murong De wept as he sent him.
proposed.after: Muyu Hu asked to ride swiftly and ascertain Murong Bao's actual circumstances. Murong De shed tears and sent him.
proposed.sourceReason: The surname in 慕輿護 is Muyu. 問寶虛實 concerns the truth about Bao’s circumstances, and 德流涕而遣之 makes De the one who weeps and sends him.
proposed.sourceChinese: 慕輿護請馳問寶虛實，德流涕而遣之。

proposed.before: He led hundreds of picked men north with Zhao Si plotting to murder Murong Bao.
proposed.after: He led several hundred picked men north after Zhao Si and plotted to kill Murong Bao.
proposed.sourceReason: 隨思而北 says that the leader followed Zhao Si north. The following plot is narrated in the same sequence. Retaining the pronoun avoids inserting a personal name absent from this unit or assigning the plot to Zhao Si.
proposed.sourceChinese: 乃率壯士數百，隨思而北，因謀殺寶。

proposed.before: Yu Hu then led several hundred stalwarts and followed Zhao Si northward and plotted to kill Murong Bao.
proposed.after: He then led several hundred brave men north after Zhao Si and plotted to kill Murong Bao.
proposed.sourceReason: The Chinese has no overt name for the subject of 乃率. The preceding unit names Muyu Hu. Keeping the subject pronominal avoids the added “Yu Hu” while preserving the following of Si, the direction north and the plot against Bao.
proposed.sourceChinese: 乃率壯士數百，隨思而北，因謀殺寶。

proposed.before: Yu Hu found no sign of Murong Bao, seized Zhao Si, and came back.
proposed.after: Muyu Hu found no sign of Murong Bao, seized Zhao Si, and came back.
proposed.sourceReason: 護 is the shortened reference following 慕輿護 in s0091. Since the existing English uses a full name here, it should carry the complete surname.

proposed.before: When Yu Hu arrived he saw nothing, seized Zhao Si, and returned.
proposed.after: When Muyu Hu arrived he saw nothing, seized Zhao Si, and returned.
proposed.sourceReason: The literal field expands 護 to a full name. The full name in s0091 is Muyu Hu, a spelling already used in s0123 and s0178.

proposed.before: It also hugs the Yangzi and Huai; waterways reach Jun, and in autumn and summer rains turn a thousand li into lakes.
proposed.after: It also lies close to the Yangzi and Huai rivers. Its waterways are open and deep, and prolonged rains in autumn and summer turn a thousand li of country into a lake.
proposed.sourceReason: 水路通浚 describes the waterways. Neither this clause nor the parallel English field supplies evidence for a place named Jun. 秋夏霖潦 describes prolonged rains and flooding in autumn and summer.
proposed.sourceChinese: 又密邇江、淮，水路通浚，秋夏霖潦，千里為湖。

proposed.before: It also hugs the Yangzi and Huai; waterways reach Jun, and in autumn and summer rains turn a thousand li into lakes.
proposed.after: It is also very near the Yangzi and Huai. The waterways are open and deep. With prolonged rains and flooding in autumn and summer, a thousand li become a lake.
proposed.sourceReason: 水路通浚 describes the waterways. Neither this clause nor the parallel English field supplies evidence for a place named Jun. 秋夏霖潦 describes prolonged rains and flooding in autumn and summer.
proposed.sourceChinese: 又密邇江、淮，水路通浚，秋夏霖潦，千里為湖。

proposed.before: Murong De summoned Bi Lü Hun in Qi commandery; when he refused, Murong Zhong attacked with twenty thousand men.
proposed.after: Murong De sent envoys to persuade Bi Lü Hun, governor of Qi Commandery. When Hun refused to comply, De sent Murong Zhong to attack him with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry.
proposed.sourceReason: 遣使喻 makes De send an envoy to Hun. It does not say he summoned Hun. The Chinese identifies Hun as governor, then gives his refusal and the second order to Zhong to lead infantry and cavalry.
proposed.sourceChinese: 德遣使喻齊郡太守避閭渾，渾不從，遣慕容鐘率步騎二萬擊之。

proposed.before: Taking Langye, Murong De drew over a hundred thousand from Xu and Yanzhou and forty thousand more north of Langye.
proposed.after: Murong De advanced and occupied Langye. More than a hundred thousand from Xu and Yan joined him, and more than forty thousand people north of Langye came to welcome him.
proposed.sourceReason: The two groups perform different actions. 附 describes the first group joining De, and 迎者四萬餘人 records more than forty thousand who came to welcome him. The current idiomatic field reduces both to numbers De drew. The literal field already records the welcome.
proposed.sourceChinese: 德進據琅邪，徐、兗之土附者十餘萬，自琅邪而北，迎者四萬餘人。

proposed.before: The rebel Bi Lü Hun's father Wei once joined Duan Kan blocking chaos on the Zi River; the grand preceptor marched east and extirpated the wicked life.
proposed.after: The rebel Bi Lü Hun's father Wei once joined Duan Kan in rebellion at Zichuan. The grand preceptor's eastern campaign put an end to that rebel's life.
proposed.sourceReason: The proclamation accuses Wei of joining Duan Kan in rebellious resistance at Zichuan. It attributes his death to the Grand Preceptor’s eastern campaign. Zizhi Tongjian 100 records that Wei was wounded and had already died when Ke sent someone to look for him. The wording does not require a personal killing by the Grand Preceptor.
proposed.sourceChinese: 逆賊辟閭渾父蔚，昔同段龕阻亂淄川，太宰東征，剿絕凶命。

proposed.before: The rebel Bi Lü Hun's father Wei once joined Duan Kan blocking chaos on the Zi River; the grand preceptor marched east and extirpated the wicked life.
proposed.after: The rebel Bi Lü Hun's father Wei once joined Duan Kan in rebellious resistance at Zichuan. The Grand Preceptor campaigned east, and the wicked man's life was cut short.
proposed.sourceReason: The proclamation accuses Wei of joining Duan Kan in rebellious resistance at Zichuan. It attributes his death to the Grand Preceptor’s eastern campaign. Zizhi Tongjian 100 records that Wei was wounded and had already died when Ke sent someone to look for him. The wording does not require a personal killing by the Grand Preceptor.
proposed.sourceChinese: 逆賊辟閭渾父蔚，昔同段龕阻亂淄川，太宰東征，剿絕凶命。
